'''Crispix''' is a brand of [[breakfast cereal]], introduced by [[Kellogg's]] in 1983. It was created specifically to compete with [[Ralston Purina]]'s [[Chex]] family of cereals, which had about $125 million in annual sales and no significant competition. By 1987, Crispix had sales of about $65 million.<ref>{{cite news |last = Steinbreder |first = H. John |url = https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/1988/08/29/70950/index.htm |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20111110115942/http://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/1988/08/29/70950/index.htm |url-status = dead |archive-date = November 10, 2011 |title =  How King Kellogg Beat the Blahs |work = [[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] |date = August 29, 1988 |access-date = July 18, 2009 }}</ref> 

Its box touts its unique composition of "Crispy [[rice]] on one side, crunchy [[Maize|corn]] on the other."<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www2.kelloggs.com/Product/ProductDetail.aspx?brand=140&product=560&cat=cereal |publisher = Kellogg's |title = Kellogg's® Crispix® Cereal |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071213145811/http://www2.kelloggs.com/Product/ProductDetail.aspx?brand=140&product=560&cat=cereal |archive-date = December 13, 2007 }}</ref> The cereal itself is in a hexagon shape. The two sides are made in a lattice pattern and connected only at the edges; the center is open. Crispix is [[kashrut|kosher]]/[[parve]].<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www.star-k.org/cons-appr-cereal.htm |title = Cereals and Their Brachos Kosher Listing |publisher = STAR-K  |access-date = February 20, 2016 }}</ref>

== Manufacturing process ==
Kellogg's has released limited information about manufacturing process that results in Crispix's unique puffed hexagon shape. According to Kellogg's, corn grits and rice are cooked separately, dried, and then rolled with a grooved roller creating a waffled appearance. The sheets of corn and rice are laid on top of each other, cut into hexagons and toasted in an oven that causes them to puff.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kellogg's|date=2020|title=How are your cereal and snacks made?|url=https://www.global.kelloggsnutrition.com/en_US/food-and-nutrition/how-is-your-cereal-made.html|url-status=live|access-date=September 23, 2021|website=Kellogg's Nutrition|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813143201/https://www.global.kelloggsnutrition.com/en_US/food-and-nutrition/how-is-your-cereal-made.html |archive-date=August 13, 2020 }}</ref>

==Flavored versions==
A variation of original Crispix introduced in late 2001 in the US known as Cinnamon Crunch Crispix was described by Kellogg's as a "[c]rispy corn and rice cereal with a [[cinnamon]] taste." Cinnamon Crunch Crispix joined a number of cereals discontinued by Kellogg's after disappointing sales.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kellogg's Cinnamon Crunch Crispix|url=http://www.mrbreakfast.com/cereal_detail.asp?id=1344|access-date=April 19, 2017|website=Mr. Breakfast}}</ref>

Honey Flavored Crispix have been sold twice in the UK, and twice have been discontinued. In Australia, Crispix is rectangular, yellow and honey-flavored. A chocolate version is sold under the name '''Coco Pops Chex'''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Coco Pops® |url=https://www.kelloggs.com.au/Home/Products/Cereal/CocoPops/tabid/323/Default.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909054325/http://www.kelloggs.com.au/Home/Products/Cereal/CocoPops/tabid/323/Default.aspx |archive-date=September 9, 2012 |access-date=January 25, 2009 |publisher=Kellogg's}}</ref> 

In some markets, Kellogg's owns the rights to the Chex name, and sells products in multiple flavors, including a green onion flavor in South Korea, the result of a marketing stunt in 2004 that asked for public input on the next flavor for the brand.<ref>{{Cite news|title=South Korea Gets Long Awaited Green Onion Chex|language=en|work=NPR.org|url=https://www.npr.org/2020/07/05/887386848/south-korea-gets-long-awaited-green-onion-chex|access-date=2021-09-23}}</ref>

==Health==
Crispix contains 3g to 5g of added sugars in some regions and 0g of dietary [[fiber]] per serving.<ref>{{Cite web |url = http://smartlabel.kelloggs.com/Product/Index/00038000035302 |title = Kellogg's® Crispix® Cereal |work = SmartLabel |publisher = Kellogg's |access-date = April 16, 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url = https://www.realcanadiansuperstore.ca/en/crispix-cereal/p/21430734_EA |title = Kelloggs Crispix Cereal 350g |publisher = [[Real Canadian Superstore]] |access-date = September 23, 2025}}</ref> The cereal received one and a half stars out of five on the Australian Government's health star ratings.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www.smh.com.au/business/retail/food-health-star-ratings-kelloggs-reveals-the-cereal-that-gets-15-stars-20150420-1mop9e.html |title = Food health star ratings: Kellogg's reveals the cereal that gets 1.5 stars |first = Esther |last = Han |newspaper = The Sydney Morning Herald |date = April 20, 2015 }}</ref>

== Popular culture ==
In 2019 on [[Logan Paul|Logan Paul's]] "Impaulsive" podcast, [[Conservatism in the United States|Conservative]] Commentator [[Ben Shapiro]] stated Crispix as his favorite cereal<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g-9TdoU4Ay8 |title=BEN SHAPIRO SILENCES LOGAN PAUL - IMPAULSIVE EP. 121 |date=2019-09-09 |last=IMPAULSIVE |access-date=2026-04-11 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

"Double Dip Crunch" a quite similar cereal also made by Kelloggs was around in the 90s. [[Cosmo Kramer|Kramer]] from the TV show [[Seinfeld]] throughout the show would mention "Double Crunch" in reference to that cereal.
